'''Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine''' (止止呂支比売命神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi-ku]], [[:en:Osaka City|Osaka City]], {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor shrine) and was formerly designated as a [[village shrine]] under the old shrine Ranking system.
== Enshrined Deities ==
* [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] 
* [[Kushinadahime|Inadahime-no-Mikoto]]
== History ==
The founding date of the shrine is unknown. The name "Todoroki" is believed to derive from the name of a bridge that once existed within the precincts. Another theory suggests that the name originates from calling [[Kushinadahime|Inadahime-no-Mikoto]] "Todorokihime." Some also attribute the name to the sound of a stream flowing through the precincts, with "todoroki" (thundering or roaring) evolving into its current form.<ref name="Osaka Health Association">[https://osaka-hk.org/posts/senjin125 Historical Overview of Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine - Osaka Health Association] Retrieved March 19, 2019</ref> Listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} as a minor shrine, it is thought to have originally served as an auxiliary shrine (okunoin) to the {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|Sumiyoshi-taisha|qid=Q705949|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha}}.
In 1220 (Shōkyū 2), during Emperor Go-Toba's pilgrimage to {{ill|Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Shrine|ja|熊野三山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shrine|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the chief priest of Sumiyoshi Taisha, Tsutsumori Tsunekuni, constructed a temporary palace (angū) in a pine grove on the shrine grounds. Known as the "Wakamatsu Gosho" (Young Pine Palace), the shrine subsequently came to be called "Wakamatsu Shrine." <ref name="Osaka City">[http://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000009370.html Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine - Osaka City] Retrieved March 19, 2019</ref>
== Shrine Grounds ==
{{right|[[File:若松行宮祉.JPG|thumb|none|Wakamatsu Temporary Palace Site]]}}
* Monument marking the site of the Wakamatsu Temporary Palace.
* Stone marker for Tensuifun Toyoura no Mikoto Shrine (Osaka City-designated cultural property).
=== Auxiliary Shrines ===
* '''Tensuifun Toyoura no Mikoto Shrine''': Enshrines {{ill|Kōjin|en|Kōjin|qid=Q6455190|lt=Sambaō Gongen}} ({{ill|Mikumari|lt=Mikumari|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|ja|水分神|2=ja|3=水分神|4=zh|5=水分神|6=sv|7=Mikumari-no-Kami|8=fr|9=Mikumari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikumari-no-Kami|qq=}}, {{ill|Okitsu-hiko-no-Mikoto|ja|奥津彦命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-hiko-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550732}}, {{ill|Okitsu-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|奥津姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-hime-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550733}}), [[Ōkuninushi]], and [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Kotoshironushi]]. This shrine, also known as Aramatsubara Arajinja, was originally located in Andatsu 2-chome, {{ill|Suminoe-ku, Osaka|en|Suminoe-ku, Osaka|qid=Q985711|lt=Suminoe-ku}}, before being relocated to Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine in 1907 (Meiji 40). It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} with no former Rank.
== Festivals ==
* '''Spring Festival (Chinka-sai)''': April 8
* '''Summer Festival''': July 11-12
* '''Autumn Festival''': October 7-8
* '''Winter Festival (Chinka-sai)''': December 8
